{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly influence mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success', perform a Chi-square test of independence (or Fisher's Exact Test if expected counts are low) instead of ANOVA, as the variable is binary (0/1), not continuous.",
    "For 'Path Efficiency', verify normality; if severely violated due to the wide range (0.0009 to 29.8) and potential skew, consider a Kruskal-Wallis H test as a non-parametric alternative.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target', 'Average Speed', and 'AD', proceed with one-way ANOVA assuming approximate normality after checking residuals."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Verify that observations within and between paradigms are independent (confirmed by experimental design with 76,655 rows from 8 mice).",
    "Normality: Check residuals for each response variable against normality (e.g., Shapiro-Wilk test, Q-Q plots). 'Success' is inherently non-normal (binary); 'Path Efficiency' may be skewed given the min/max spread.",
    "Homogeneity of Variances: Conduct Levene's test or Bartlett's test for equal variances across the five paradigm groups for all continuous response variables.",
    "Sample Size Balance: Note the imbalance in group sizes (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846); ANOVA is robust to moderate imbalance, but large imbalance requires checking variance homogeneity strictly.",
    "Outliers: Inspect boxplots for extreme values in 'Time-to-Target' (max 201) and 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.8) that could inflate variance."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA yields a significant p-value (p < 0.05), conduct post-hoc pairwise comparisons.",
    "Use Tukey's HSD (Honest Significant Difference) test for all continuous variables ('Time-to-Target', 'Path Efficiency', 'Average Speed', 'AD') to control the Family-Wise Error Rate.",
    "For 'Success', use a post-hoc pairwise comparison of proportions (e.g., pairwise proportion tests with Bonferroni correction) following the Chi-square test.",
    "Specifically investigate the 'Sham' group against others, given the summary shows a notably lower mean Success (0.273) and higher Time-to-Target (4.68) compared to other paradigms.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., Eta-squared for ANOVA, Cramer's V for Chi-square) to quantify the magnitude of paradigm effects."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on summary statistics, 'Sham' is expected to show significantly worse performance than other paradigms: lower Success (0.27 vs ~0.68-0.78), higher Time-to-Target (4.68 vs ~2.6-3.1), lower Average Speed (10.7 vs ~12.0-12.8), and lower Path Efficiency (0.31 vs ~0.43-0.50).",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion) is expected to be significantly lower in 'Sham' (0.236) compared to 'Combined' (0.399) and 'Bright Visual Only' (0.387), suggesting less variable or more constrained movement in the control group, or potentially a data artifact given the interpretation of AD.",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only are expected to be statistically similar to each other and to Combined, but distinct from Sham and potentially Bright Visual Only.",
    "Path Efficiency shows a clear gradient, with Sham having the lowest mean (0.308) and Bright Visual Only/Combined having the highest (~0.50)."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846) may affect the power of the test for the Sham group and the validity of variance assumptions.",
    "The variable 'Path Efficiency' has an extremely wide range (0.0009 to 29.8), which may indicate a distribution heavily skewed by outliers or a measurement scale issue, violating ANOVA normality assumptions.",
    "The interpretation of 'AD' as angular dispersion relies on the assumption that higher values indicate greater dispersion; the summary shows 'Sham' has the lowest AD, which might contradict the expectation of random/noise in a sham condition if higher dispersion is expected, requiring careful domain validation.",
    "Data is aggregated at the row level; individual mouse-level random effects (repeated measures) are not explicitly modeled in this one-way ANOVA plan, potentially inflating Type I error if multiple trials per mouse are correlated.",
    "Missing data is reported as 0, but the filtering process (78687 to 76655 rows) should be reviewed to ensure no systematic bias was introduced by the row filters."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures within the 8 mice, providing more robust inference than a standard one-way ANOVA."
}
